It is scientifically impossible to turn pea soup back into whole peas.
When you cook split peas to make soup, they undergo two irreversible chemical and physical changes:
Starch Gelatinization: The starch granules inside the peas absorb water, swell, and burst, permanently breaking down their structure into a creamy liquid.
Cell Wall Breakdown: The heat completely dissolves the pectin and cell walls holding the peas together, meaning the physical "building blocks" of the individual peas no longer exist.
Because these changes alter the peas at a molecular level, you cannot un-cook or reassemble them.
If you are trying to rescue a batch of soup, let me know:
Is the soup too thick or mushy, and you want more texture?
Are you looking for ways to add whole peas back in as a garnish?
I can help you adjust the texture to make it more appetizing!
